title: Sorting out the order of his schools and school bands
summary: Barnet and Willard untangle Berkeley-Irving, Riverdale, Blair, New Trier; he played tuba at Blair and soprano at Riverdale.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: It was school you weren't happy with, is that right?

No, on the contrary. I mean I was very happy with the school, but I liked New York. This was at the time just a little bit too rural for my tastes. Because It was quite rural at that time. Now I guess it's all built in like everything else is.
So you went to -- the last school you went to was the New Trier School, not Burkley Irving.
No, I went to Burkley Irving after New Trier.
Oh, I see.
You see, I came -- let's get this -- yeah -- no, no. We've got it -- we've got Blair Academy in there someplace.
All right. That's I think the only school name I've read in any of the material about you, is Blair Academy.
Well, that was in 1926. I think I went to Blair after the New Trier -- no, I was at Blair before New Trier. That's right.
And Riverdale before Blair?
Oh, Riverdale was -- oh, yes, definitely. It would go in this order. Burkley Irving, Riverdale, then Blair, then New Trier, and then back to Burkley.
I see. Okay. And did anyplace besides Riverdale have a school band?
Well, all of them had bands.
Did you play in all of them?
I didn't play in the New Trier band. But I played in the band -- I played tuba in the Blair band.
Oh. And soprano at Riverdale.
At Riverdale.
And what did you play at Burkley Irving?
Well, they didn't have a band.
Oh.
They --
You wouldn't have had time anyway, if you were --
No, I was already -- the second time -- I was much too young to play in any band the first time in Burkley and the second time I was already making it out in the real thing.
I see. So your first experience with soprano was at Riverdale.
Yeah, around in 1922.
And then by the time you were 16 you had a tenor? Is that right?
Yes. Yes.
